subject: Agriculture
title: The Birth of Agriculture
description: A 1-minute de-risking session on The Birth of Agriculture.

hook.text: For 200,000 years, humans hunted and gathered. Then, about 12,000 years ago, everything changed.

buildup.text: In the Fertile Crescent, people began planting wild wheat and barley instead of just collecting them.

discovery.text: Farming let people stay in one place. Permanent villages appeared for the first time in human history.

twist.text: Early farmers were shorter and sicker than hunter-gatherers. Farming was harder on the body.

climax.text: But farming fed more people per acre. Population grew, and there was no going back.

punchline.text: Agriculture made civilization possible—at a cost.

quiz.question: Where did agriculture first emerge about 12,000 years ago?
